content.thinking:
I'm laying out the postmortem: metrics stopped at 02:35, and the deploy at 02:35:15 renamed the metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics`. The ServiceMonitor at c3c36da still selects the old port name, while the production values at that commit already use the new one.

I'm checking the earlier deploy at 22:35:15 and whether the metrics read up to 02:34 shows the service was healthy with it in place, since those samples suggest metrics were still being collected then.

I'm settling on the root cause: the deploy renamed the metrics port to `http-metrics`, but the ServiceMonitor still selects the endpoint by the old name `metrics`, so it matches nothing and Prometheus has no target to scrape. I'm also ruling out the earlier 22:35 deploy, since metrics were still being collected up to 02:34 with that version in place, and checking that the zero-flag changes point only to Argus.

I'm reordering the causal chain so the symptom comes first, then the reason Prometheus had nothing to scrape. The rename itself is the next link, and I'm checking that the scrape config was never updated alongside it.

I'm working out how the scrape selector and the renamed port fit together, and checking whether a rename alone was enough to break the scrape. The config that selects the port by name never got updated alongside the deploy.

I'm now checking the contributing factors: the scrape config's port name is never checked against the values file, so nothing caught the mismatch before the change shipped. I'm also noting that the operator quietly treats a name matching no port as an empty target list, with no alert on a zero target count, so the gap was only caught later by the metrics-absent alert.

I'm weighing whether an alert on an empty target list would have caught the gap sooner than the metrics-absent alert did, and I'm treating the missing alert as its own contributing factor.

I'm now looking at whether the estate-wide convention might have caught the rename, though that part of the thinking trails off there.

I'm settling on what the rest of the write-up should cover: a check that the port names agree on every change to deploy/, so a change to one side fails without the other.

I'm settling on the remaining action items, and I'm ruling out an audit of other services renamed under the convention, since nothing in the record ties that to a contributing factor.

I'm drafting the action items now: a deploy of the merged fix to io-shop so metrics resume, and I'm weighing whether that counts as a check, since it only mitigates the root cause and answers none of the contributing factors.

I'm noting that the Investigator Agent tied the onset to the deploy by reading its diff and its rollout across all replicas, and that Argus declined to roll back the deliberate port rename, taking no mitigation and leaving the convention in place. I'm also seeing that the Code-Fix Agent proposed a draft pull request, and that Argus checked the flag history.

I'm checking whether the scrape config's comment, which tells the reader to keep a key path in step with the values file, actually names a path that no longer exists after the deploy.

I'm settling on the assumptions: the metric gap began with the rename, though the onset is only dated to its minute, which starts before the deploy's exact time, and I'm checking the ServiceMonitor's selector against the renamed port.

I'm checking that the shop's metrics port name matches what the scrape config expects, and noting the rendered Service takes its port name from the values file. I'm also marking the contributing factor about a failing check as having no addressing action items yet.

I'm checking the step-4 claim against the ruled-out causes: the earlier deploy and the zero-flag changes don't account for the gap, and the change only edited the production values file while the scrape config kept the old port name.

action_items.item: Make the check that the ServiceMonitor's endpoint port name matches the metrics port name in values-production.yaml a required CI gate on every change to deploy/, so a rename that updates only one file is blocked.
Add an alert that fires when the io-shop ServiceMonitor resolves to no scrape targets.
Route the MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop to the on-call rotation so it pages a person.
Once the scrape port fix is merged, deploy a revision that carries it to io-shop.

causal_chain.step: Nobody using the shop was seen to have anything go wrong. What was seen instead: the shop's metrics stopped arriving, and the series went absent rather than crossing a threshold.

The metrics stopped because Prometheus had no target to scrape. At the revision that was running, the ServiceMonitor picks the endpoint by the port name `metrics` (S1), and no port at that revision has that name: the metrics port is named `http-metrics` (S2). The scrape config itself says that a name matching no port gives an empty target list, not an error.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 2c8f7311966cf37dee314695fe0060867e1ca954: metrics were still collected with it in place, up to the minute before the onset.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider's history shows no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before {T16.4}.

causal_chain.step: No port was named `metrics` any more because the deploy of revision c3c36da3c66c07707f227b7e70b26813083061f3 at {P2.1} renamed every port to the `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` convention, including the metrics port, from `metrics` to `http-metrics` (D1). As of {T13.1}, all replicas were running that revision.
The rename broke scraping because the change edited only deploy/values-production.yaml and left the scrape config still selecting the port by its old name.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A planned renaming of the shop's network ports to a platform-wide naming rule also renamed the port the monitoring system collects the shop's measurements from, and the monitoring setup, which finds that port by its name, was not changed to match, so it had nothing to collect.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that the port name the ServiceMonitor selects agrees with the metrics port name in values-production.yaml. The scrape config at the revision that ran says that nothing checks this, so a change to only one of the two files could ship.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check that failed on the mismatch would have stopped the rename from going out without a matching change to the scrape config, so the metrics would not have stopped.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: When the ServiceMonitor selects a port name that matches no port, the operator does not raise an error; it gives an empty target list. No alert on an empty scrape target list was seen, so the gap was found only by the MetricsAbsent rule once samples had been missing for its window.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: An alert or error on a ServiceMonitor with no targets would have caught the mismatch as soon as the rollout finished, without waiting for the metrics to be absent for the whole window.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been told directly and could have taken up the open fix and its deploy sooner, shortening the time the shop ran unwatched.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the deployment's diff and how far it had rolled out, finding the metrics port rename running on every replica.
Argus checked the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone else.
Argus declined to roll back the port rename, a change made on purpose, and took no mitigation that would undo it.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #535 for a person to review.

input.root_cause: The deployment renamed the metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics` in deploy/values-production.yaml, but deploy/scrape.yaml at that revision still picks the endpoint to scrape by the name `metrics`. The ServiceMonitor selects by port name, and a name that matches no port does not raise an error to the operator. It just gives an empty target list, so Prometheus had nothing to scrape.
input.still_at_risk: Until a deploy carries a matching scrape port name, io-shop's metrics stay uncollected, and any real fault in the shop could go unseen by alerts that work from those metrics.
input.symptom: Shoppers saw nothing wrong, but the shop's metrics stopped arriving
